result.text: Title: Contract For your contract project you need parts from several web shops.
In order to find out which web shop has the right parts, you have to query them all, and find out how much they can deliver, at which price, and how long it will take.

If one shop has not enough parts, order from several shops.
Always use the cheapest parts.

When the first parts arrive you start building.
Sometimes you have to reorder parts.
If your stock (for a single part) falls below 5, you reorder (the cheapest), if it falls below 3 you reorder again (the fastest).
If it is zero, you write a mail to your friends, complaining about the webshops.

Title: Contract

For your contract project you need parts from several web shops.
In order to find out which web shop has the right parts, you have to query them all, and find out how much they can deliver, at which price, and how long it will take.
Create a list of parts that you order from each shop.
If one shop has not enough  parts, order from several shops.
Always use the cheapest parts.
The parts arrive in batches in a random order, typically they are +/- 2 days earlier/later.
When the first parts arrive you start building.
Sometimes you have to reorder parts.
If your stock (for a single part) falls below 5, you reorder (the cheapest), if it falls below 3 you reorder again (the fastest).
If it is zero, you write a mail to your friends, complaining about the webshops.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an exclusive split when exactly one data-based alternative runs. Add supported conditions and at most one default fallback.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.
Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.

result.rule: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives for where or how an item is handled: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and separate alternative paths, then merge them before any shared next step.
When the description states a decision with multiple distinct outcomes: Model the decision as a gateway and connect it by a sequence flow to every described outcome branch.

When the description states that the same process can be initiated through mutually exclusive alternative channels or methods: Model the alternatives with an exclusive gateway after the start event, with each outcome representing one alternative.

When the description makes an action conditional on whether a stated condition holds: Model the condition as a control-flow decision with alternative outgoing paths, so the action is taken only on the applicable path; do not use a gateway with only one incoming and one outgoing sequence flow.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant enters information or other inputs as a distinct action: Model that action as a separate activity in the appropriate sequence; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.

When the description says to send work to another participant and request changes until an acceptance condition is met, without describing distinct incoming messages for each iteration: Model one response-receiving activity or message-catching event before the acceptance decision, and loop the exchange through that decision; do not add separate receiving elements for inferred intermediate responses.

When the description says that a participant carries out an activity over a period before making a later decision: Model the activity before the decision; do not use an event marking the period's end as a substitute for the activity.

When the description says a review determines whether a stated outcome may proceed: Model the review as an activity and the approval as a decision; connect the approved branch to the stated outcome without adding a separate approval activity unless the description states one.
